Non-Surgical Breast Enlargement

Do Breast Enlargement Creams, Pills and Massage Actually Work?

Creams, supplements, massage routines and pumps are widely sold as alternatives to surgery. Here is what the evidence does and does not support.

Home/Non-Surgical Breast Enlargement/Do Breast Enlargement Creams, Pills and Massage Actually Work?

Search for ways to enlarge breasts and you will find creams, capsules, herbal supplements, massage routines and pumping devices, often with dramatic promises. This page explains what these products claim and what is actually known.

Creams and gels

These are applied to the skin and are generally cosmetic moisturisers. There is no reliable evidence that a cream applied to the surface can grow breast tissue. Some may leave skin feeling smoother, which can be mistaken for a change in size.

Pills and herbal supplements

Many products claim to contain plant compounds with oestrogen-like activity. Evidence that they produce lasting breast growth is weak, and products can vary in strength and content. Hormone-active substances can affect periods, mood and other systems, and are not appropriate for everyone, including people with hormone-sensitive conditions. Speak to a doctor before taking any supplement for this purpose. See breast enlargement safety.

Massage and chest exercises

Massage may feel pleasant, but there is no good evidence that it increases breast volume. Chest exercises build the pectoral muscles beneath the breast. A stronger chest wall may change the look of the upper chest, but exercise does not enlarge breast tissue itself, and fat loss can reduce breast size.

Suction and pumping devices

These claim to stimulate growth. Evidence of a lasting increase is lacking, and they can cause bruising or skin irritation.

What actually changes breast size?

Breast size changes naturally with weight, hormones, pregnancy, breastfeeding and age. Only medical procedures such as implants or fat transfer are designed to add volume, and each carries its own risks. Read breast enlargement without surgery for a method-by-method review.

How to judge a claim

  • Is there independent research, not just testimonials?
  • Is the product registered or approved for this use by a recognised regulator?
  • Does it list ingredients and doses clearly?
  • Does it promise guaranteed results or a specific cup-size increase? If so, be sceptical.

Key takeaway

There is no proven cream, pill, massage or device that lastingly enlarges breasts. If you are unhappy with your breast size, a conversation with a qualified clinician is a better starting point than a product.

Questions about creams, pills and massage

Massage may reduce tension or feel relaxing, but there is no reliable evidence that it produces lasting breast growth.

Not necessarily. Products vary in content and strength, and hormone-active ingredients can affect the body in ways that matter for some people. Check with a doctor before using them.
